summary: Hugh B. Urban works in religious studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago (~1992-1998) under Wendy Doniger, Bruce Lincoln, and Tony K. Stewart, and became Associate Professor at Ohio State University around 1998.

Hugh Edward Richardson was a Tibetologist who studied at Keble College, Oxford (~1923-1927). He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1930-1947), founded the Tibet Society (1959), and was an Honorary Fellow at the British Academy (1952) and Keble College (1981).
Hugh Gray studied at Battersea Grammar School and worked in Indology and other fields. Around 1961, he held a post at SOAS University of London and was a lecturer at the University of London.

Hugh J. Silverman was a philosopher who earned his doctorate from Stanford University (~1969-1973). He became professor at Stony Brook University in 1974, directed the IAPL (~1980-2013), and held Fulbright Chairs in Vienna (2000-2001, 2009-2010).

Hugo David is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who earned his PhD from École Pratique des Hautes Études in 2012. After a fellowship at the University of Cambridge (2013-2014), he became a permanent member of École française d'Extrême-Orient in 2015.
Hugo Enomiya-Lassalle worked in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He served at Sophia University (~1938-1945) and studied under the traditional teacher Koun Yamada (~1960-1989).
Huidi Zeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University, where she studied under MA supervisor Yi-hsun Huang (attested 2011).
Huifeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2007) and held a post at the University of Hong Kong.

Huimin is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1986-1992). He held posts at Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies, Taipei National University of the Arts (~1992-2022), and served as President of Dharma Drum Institute (~2014-2022).
Huishan Lin is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under Kuo-wei Liu, Mansheng, Miaoguan, and Ruying.
Huiwen Zhuang is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under Kirill Solonin and studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun.
Huiyu Zhang is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo and served as a lecturer at Dongguk University (attested 1996).

Humberto Maturana was a philosopher and biologist who studied at the University of Chile, UCL, and Harvard (doctoral degree 1956-1958). He was an assistant professor at the University of Chile (1960) and founded Instituto Matríztica in 2000.

Hung Wu is an art historian and sinologist who earned his PhD from Harvard (~1980-1987). He taught at Harvard (1990) and became Harrie A. Vanderstappen Distinguished Service Professor of Art History at the University of Chicago in 1994.
Hung-Yi Yang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at the University of Sydney under doctoral supervisor Mark Allon (attested 2013).

Huston Smith was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who earned a PhD from the University of Chicago (~1940-1945). He served as professor at MIT (1958-1973) and Syracuse University (1973-1983).

Huynh Kim Lan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master Degree of Arts at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under thesis advisers Phra Suthithammanuwat and Veerachart Nimanong (attested 2010).
Huynh Thi Ha Vy is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College, studying under Kapila Abhayawansa.

Hwansoo Kim is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who held posts as a professor at Duke University (attested 2017) and professor of religious studies at Yale University (attested 2026).

Hyakudai Sakamoto was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1948-1951). He held positions at Tokyo University of Pharmacy and Life Sciences (~1962-1968), Aoyama Gakuin University (~1968-1999), and The Open University of Japan (~1999-2004).
